sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5474.21 .B73 2024
sources.quote: On Totoli (Lauje's sister language, covered by the same 1991 penultimate-stress statement): 'Totoli shows no evidence of tonal specifications at the level of the word; the language does not make use of word stress nor of lexical tone ... tonal specifications are assigned exclusively at the level of the intonational phrase and are associated with their right-edge boundary.' Also: 'The absence of (post)lexical stress ... may likewise be found in many other languages of the region, as the results from Totoli suggest.' Lauje is never mentioned (0 hits).
sources.locator: Abstract/introduction (front matter p. iv-v and ch. 1, p. 9-10); experimental summary before sec. 3.2
sources.note: Instrumental production+perception study of Lauje's closest documented relative, which Himmelmann 1991 described with the identical penultimate rule; finds no word stress in Totoli. Silent on Lauje, but the natural source for a 'caution' note on the record (Lauje's paragogic-vowel antepenult pattern is itself an argument for word-level stress that Totoli lacks, since Totoli has no paragoge, 1991: 52).

sources.quote: Same author, 27 years later, on the area generally: 'what has often been described as regular penultimate stress is in fact the regular occurrence of a rising-falling edge tone combination at the end of intonational phrases ... it is not advisable to assume the existence of lexical stress in a particular Austronesian language without further validation', but adds: 'it may be the case that there is sufficient evidence for stress-like distinctions in some languages of Sulawesi, in particular Central Sulawesi languages, as briefly discussed in Himmelmann & Kaufman (2018)'. sources.note: The 1991 author's current position on whether western Austronesian 'penultimate stress' is word stress or a phrase-final edge tone; Himmelmann 2018: 351 (downloaded) says Central Sulawesi languages may be genuine exceptions and points to this chapter for the discussion -- needed to know whether he still stands by word-level penultimate stress for Lauje/Tomini-Tolitoli after Bracks's Totoli results.

sources.note: The only other Lauje-specific phonology paper (23 pp, same fieldworker); treats exactly the interaction our 'strict penultimate' coding abstracts away from (paragogic /e/ yielding surface antepenultimate stress, labong/labonge) and would settle whether the paragoge is post-lexical (keeping 'strict') or lexical (making the rule penult-with-exceptions).
